nodes.label: Costs, Compensation and Post-Trial Orders
nodes.summary: Costs orders, compensation, restitution, post-sentence orders.

nodes.label: Costs in Criminal Cases
nodes.summary: Costs in Criminal Cases Ordinance (Cap 492): Court may award costs to prosecution or defence. Defence costs: may be ordered if defendant acquitted and no sufficient reason for prosecution, or if proceedings not instituted in good faith (s.3). Prosecution costs: may be ordered against convicted defendant (s.7). Costs must be reasonable; taxed if necessary.

nodes.label: Costs in Criminal Cases Ordinance (Cap 492) s.3
nodes.summary: Defence costs may be ordered if acquitted and no sufficient reason for prosecution.

nodes.label: Costs in Criminal Cases Ordinance (Cap 492) s.7
nodes.summary: Prosecution costs may be ordered against convicted defendant.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Chen Keen (No 2)
nodes.summary: Costs after jury discharge before verdict.

nodes.label: Compensation Orders
nodes.summary: Under Cap 221 s.73, court may order compensation from offender for personal injury, loss or damage. Not a full civil damages assessment; must be quantum ascertainable.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.73
nodes.summary: Compensation order for personal injury, loss or damage.

nodes.label: Restitution and Disposal of Property
nodes.summary: Cap 221 ss.102-106A: Court may order return of stolen property, disposal of exhibits, forfeiture of instrumentalities.

nodes.label: Criminal Bankruptcy Orders
nodes.summary: Under Cap 221 s.84A (check status) or under Bankruptcy Ordinance — essentially now unused.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.84A
nodes.summary: Criminal bankruptcy orders (may be repealed; check status).

nodes.label: Post-Sentence Orders
nodes.summary: Suspended sentence; supervision order for young offenders; probation.
